It felt to me like the chef got confused between making a sweet dish and a main course. I paid ~₹450 for what tasted like a bland, uninspired dessert -definitely not a proper kofta!

reviews:
["{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Neel:Evergreen
With neel full of surprises a genie out of the box displaying unique foods everytime u come back amazed
The ongoing bottomless brunch is of biryani & kebabs till end of august 2019
A shout-out to all biryani & kebab lovers.From lucknow to hyderabad the preparation of biryani changes
Ambience:Classy yet subtle.Full of sunshine and greenery.U barely feel ur in mumbai.But ur & how?Right in the ♥️ of mumbai when entire race course as eye-candy and lovely looking stallions 🐎trotting away for daily practise
Neel Fruit Punch:Burst of fruity flavours.Khus Makes It Unique
Malta Orange & Mint Mojito:Zingy!Tangy!Full bodied citrus flavours.Whoosh!Takes away tht tiredness
Brocolli malai kali mirch:Malai brocolli tht too tandoor sounds yum & delicious.This had creaminess from the cheese & cream.It is tandoored to give the charred edges but cuts as soft as butter.
Lotus stem tikki(nadru ke shammi kebab:Takes u to the heaven on earth kashmir.With my upteen trips to the beautiful city memories hit me with moist eyes.These cute rounds make a delicious starter.The fiery greenchillies,redchillies,garam masala with onions & a bit of chat masala add zing just a hint.Goes very well with the served green chutney
Must mentions are all 3chutneys green chutney,pineapple chutney,papaya chutney.They give equal importance to the accompaniments.All these three chutneys are paired very well with the starters
Paneer charbagh:An awadhi tandoor delight.The green chutney makes it superbly delicious
Dakshini aloo:This enhances the south indian flavours.Bold flavours.If ur a potato lover this has even chatpata ness to it
Mains:Teekhi Paneer Lucknowi Biryani:Awadhi biryani paired best with burhani raita.The hint of nutmeg with medley of whole spices hint of garlic and paneer well marinated.This has flavours in every bite
Kathal(Jackfruit)ki Kerala Biryani:Quite popular in the state of kerala.An unusual biryani and good meat teazer for vegetarians.The tang of the tomatoes add another dimenson.The whole spices have fragrance in each bite.These deep-fried jewels are buttery soft
Mushroom Biryani:Chettinad Mushroom biryani.The gingergarlic paste and full-bodied whole spices make this a well-rounded biryani.Mushroom is a star throughout
Accompaniments:Burhani Raita:A creamy raita from hyderabad cuisine flavoured with redchilli & garlic
Kasundi & Rosemary Raita:The pungent flavours will not over-power of mustard as rosemary comes as a huge welcome enhancing the tastes further
Kairi & Pudina Raita:When u want an extraordinary raita this one is the one.The black salt,redchilli powder & sugar make it unique
Plaincurd,Kachumbar are served
Kabul ki dal:Afghan dal.A little thicker.Melt in the mouth dal!Creamy,buttery soft lentils
Mirch ka salan:Authentic hyderabadi recipe.Delicious side dish.With flavours of onion seeds and tamarind & fenugreekseeds.The dry coconut  with peanuts and sesame seeds add another dimension
Desserts:Kulfi falooda:Rich & Delicious.With sabja,rose syrup and creamy kulfi.Winner!
Chocolate Brownie:Delicious gooey chocolate.Light & fluffy!
In non-veg the starters were murgh kali mirch tikka,gosht ki shikampuri,parsi chicken farcha achari prawn samosa.In biryani's there were charminar mutton biryani.doodhiya murgh biryani,prawn malwani barley biryani & tar korma
Should u visit?If ur a biryani and kebab lover.Absolutely Yes!

It is one of those restaurants in Borivali that continues to feel like home because of its food and hospitality.

This time, we began our meal with a bowl of Chicken Manchow Soup. It was served hot, and I enjoyed how it had a bold, flavorful taste without being overpowering. For starters, we ordered Veg Seekh Kebab, Mutton Seekh Kebab, and Chicken Pahadi Tikka. The Veg Seekh Kebab was nice, cooked well, and had the perfect earthy flavour. The Mutton Seekh Kebab was outstanding. It had a silky texture, was well-seasoned, and paired beautifully with the chutney. It was not chewy at all, and I really liked how smooth it felt with every bite. The Chicken Pahadi Tikka was equally good. The chicken was tender, juicy, and cooked with a light smokiness that made it enjoyable.

For the mains, I ordered Jeera Rice with Dal Tadka. The dal had a nice garlic tempering with the right amount of cumin, and together with the rice it felt wholesome and comforting. It went really well with the Tandoori Roti, which was crisp on the edges and soft in the middle. The Chicken Triple Schezwan Fried Rice was the last dish. It was mildly spiced, had a smoky taste from the wok, and the flavours were balanced in a way that made it enjoyable till the last bite.

It was the highlight of the evening. The chicken inside was fresh and well-cooked, and every bite reminded me why I have loved this dish here for years.

The food at Silver Coin Family Restaurant and Bar is consistently good, and the staff make the experience even better. They are polite, attentive, and always welcoming. Their extensive range of starters is incredibly delicious. Both AC and outdoor seating areas available. Please note that smoking is only permitted in the outdoor section.

The seating area is utilized efficiently, making the most of the available space. However, the tables are positioned quite close together, which can make the space feel a bit congested. Despite this, the overall atmosphere remains lively and inviting.

The only drawback is that the service can be a bit slow, especially during peak hours when it gets very crowded. Be prepared to wait, but trust me, it's worth it.

I will recommend to try lemon chicken and obviously chakali with schezwan sauce as combination tastes really nice., name_person=Janhavi Raut}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹200–400, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=a year ago, review=If you’re looking for an affordable spot to drink and chill in Bandra, Yacht Bar & Restaurant is worth checking out – but don’t go expecting luxury. It’s a no-frills, budget-friendly place that’s been around for ages and is popular, especially with the younger crowd.

Ambience and Crowd:
We visited on a weekend around 11:00 PM and the place was packed. It’s quite congested, so don’t expect much elbow room. We had to wait for 20 minutes before getting a table, which wasn’t surprising given its reputation for cheap drinks. They have two sections – AC and non-AC. We opted for the AC section, which was relatively comfortable.

Service and Drinks:
The staff was polite and fast, which was impressive given the crowd. The liquor here is very affordable, which explains why it’s so popular. It’s perfect if you’re on a tight budget and looking for a place to hang out with friends.

Food Experience:
The food, however, was disappointing. We tried the Chicken Crispy, a recommendation from the waiter, but it was dry and tough to chew. On the bright side, we enjoyed the chakli with Schezwan sauce.

Facilities:
Despite the heavy crowd, the washrooms were clean and there’s enough parking space available, which is a big plus in Bandra.

Final Thoughts:
Yacht Bar & Restaurant isn’t for everyone, but it’s a great option if you’re looking for a budget-friendly place to drink and chill. The crowd and ambiance might not be ideal for a quiet evening and the food could use improvement, but for cheap booze and a lively vibe, it gets the job done., name_person=Alok Shettigar}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Tasty Food Loved the vibe and the staff the waiter was helping Quality place 💯}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Good service, food ok,booze genuine days the main thing..}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Great food, cheap prices on liquor, convenient location, helpful staff}"]

The ambiance is comfortable, and the professional staff ensures you have a pleasant experience.

What sets this place apart is their outstanding service and flavorful food. For those who enjoy a drink, the bar provides a variety of free chakna options, including boiled peanuts, salted peanuts, chakli with mint chutney, garlic chiwda, and dry chickpeas—an excellent touch for alcohol enthusiasts.

The half-plate option for starters is a thoughtful addition, allowing you to enjoy a variety of dishes without stretching your budget. We tried the Chicken Crispy (₹120, ideal for two) and the Banjara Kebab (₹160), both of which were delicious and worth every penny.

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹400–600, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations not required, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=a month ago, review=Lata Restaurant in Kandivali is one of those classic local gems that serve comforting, flavorful food with generous portions and good consistency. The place has a homely vibe — nothing too fancy, but perfect if you’re looking for satisfying North Indian, Punjabi, or Chinese dishes without spending too much.

The food quality is impressive for the price. The curries are rich and well-balanced, especially the Paneer Butter Masala and Dal Tadka — both are fresh, not overly oily, and cooked with authentic spices. The tandoori rotis and butter naan are soft and served hot. Chinese options like Veg Triple Rice and Paneer Chilly are flavorful with that perfect desi-Chinese touch.

Service is quick and polite, even during rush hours. The staff is attentive and always ready to customize spice levels or suggest dishes.

Ambience is clean and simple — not high-end but comfortable for families and small groups. The restaurant is well-maintained and hygienic, though the seating area can get a bit crowded during weekends.

Value for money: Excellent. The portion sizes justify the price, making it a great everyday dining spot in Kandivali.

What I liked:

Consistent taste and freshness

Quick service

Budget-friendly pricing

Variety in menu

What can improve:

Limited parking space

My recent visit to Myra Dining and Bar was nothing short of phenomenal, and it has instantly become one of my favorite spots. The entire experience, from the service to the food, was absolutely perfect and deserves a wholehearted five stars.

Service (5/5):
From the moment we stepped in, we were treated with such warm hospitality. The staff was incredibly attentive, professional, and courteous. They were knowledgeable about the menu, offered great recommendations, and ensured our glasses were never empty. The service was prompt without ever feeling rushed, striking the perfect balance that truly elevates a dining experience.

Food (5/5):
The food was the star of the show! Each dish we ordered was a masterpiece of flavour and presentation.

Chicken Mastani Kebab: This was an absolute revelation. The chicken was incredibly tender and succulent, coated in a rich, creamy, and flavourful marinade that simply melted in the mouth. A must-try for any kebab lover.

Bombil Chilly Dry: As a fan of seafood, I was blown away by this dish. The Bombil was perfectly crispy on the outside while remaining delicate and soft inside. It was tossed in a wonderfully balanced chilly sauce that had the right amount of spice and zest without overpowering the fish. Utterly addictive!

Paneer Tikka Biryani: This was one of the best biryanis I have ever had. The aromatic, long-grain basmati rice was layered perfectly with fragrant spices and generous, smoky chunks of paneer tikka. It was flavourful, rich, and cooked to perfection.

Cheese Garlic Naan: The perfect companion to our meal. It was soft, fluffy, and oozing with the perfect amount of cheese and garlic flavour.

Desserts (Custard and Brownie with Ice Cream): The perfect end to a perfect meal. The Custard was classic, creamy, and silky smooth with just the right level of sweetness. The Brownie with Ice Cream was pure indulgence – a warm, fudgy, and decadent brownie perfectly complemented by a scoop of cold, creamy ice cream.

Overall:
Myra Dining and Bar is a fantastic establishment that gets everything right. It's the ideal place for a special occasion, a family dinner, or just when you want to treat yourself to some truly exceptional food. We left feeling completely satisfied and impressed. We will definitely be back and will be recommending Myra to all our friends and family. It was a delightful afternoon spent with great cocktails and surprising fusion of flavors and concepts. We were a party of six, so we could experience a lot on the menu and barring perhaps a couple of the dishes, every other dish was simply delectable and yum! There isn’t a “one” dish that I can single out as the highlight, there were multiple of them. Among the cocktails we tried:
·         Tamarind Whisky Shake – just a hint of the sweet sourness from the tamarind to add the kick but did not lose the character of the whisky
·         Waiting List – Gin based, curry leaf salt flavored, quite innovative in terms of the flavors
·         Stranger cocktail – Refreshing and again flavor packed
For drinks we also had the IPA, Belgian Wit and a green apple mocktail (green flag). The beers were nice but the mocktail was ok, especially compared to the bursts of flavors we were experiencing from the other drinks. A lot of what we ate was all simply superb and sent us down a flavor packed, surprise filled road! I mean – who would have thunk “kadi patta khakra” can taste that good!!! On the flip side, some of the dishes in our opinion missed the mark or were simply not to our palate like the Prawn Malai Curry (felt very watery and one could only taste the galangal and not much else), Prawn Pani Puri (just felt like a bit of strange juxtaposition in terms of flavors) and the fish pulimunchi (which was good in terms of flavor but simply wasn’t pulimunchi). 2. Handling Personal Items: Later, while a waiter was serving food, he picked up our personal belongings from the table and put them on the couch corner without our permission. This was extremely unprofessional.
3. Forced to Rush Out (The Climax): After dinner, we had just cut and served the cake when another waiter, named Shahdud, came to our table. He instructed us that he was there to clean the table, even though we were still eating the cake.

* He insisted, saying, "I want to clear the table, it's closing time." (The restaurant officially closes at 4 AM, and this happened at 3 AM.)
* I pointed out the closing time and mentioned that other people were still there (including a large family with many kids who were exploring the place, and they were not told to leave). I also explained that we were young women waiting for family to pick us up and needed time to finish up.
* His rude response was that he had a lot of work to do and had to clean up so he could come back to work the next morning. He basically told us to leave immediately so he could finish his work quickly.
👎 Conclusion
We were not spending hours there; they started trying to get rid of us almost as soon as we arrived. The staff's behavior was completely unacceptable, especially since our bill was substantial.
Later, I messaged Noomam Hussain, who manages their social media and the Mira Road branch. He apologized but then ignored me (left me "on seen") after I told him I planned to write a review.
I will be sharing this unacceptable behavior on my social media @Barkat_resin_. We came across this recently opened place called Baroke at Grant Road.

Location is bit confusing with maps, however the manager helped us in finding it very quickly. Place is situated on the first floor of Krishna palace Hotel.

Ambience and decor actually cheered up our mood. It is a perfect party and chill out place for you and your gang. Place is spacious with limited yet comfortable sitting area with a dance floor.

Coming to the food, food menu is not so lengthy with some veg and non veg quick bite items. We loved all the dishes that we tried. The Bar menu offers some really good options in cocktails.

We totally loved phuljhadi chicken tikka, fish tikka and baby corn tempura. Also the white sauce pasta for main course was creamy and delicious.

From Bar menu we tried Cucumber rosemary gin tonic, Gauva Daiquiri and Coffee caipirinha. We totally enjoyed our drinks. All of them were refreshing.

Baroke sets up a perfect weekend mood with good food, great music and classy ambience.

Totally recommended.

Located in Vile Parle East, this restaurant and bar serves some amazingly fresh and quality dishes. The primary cuisine served is North Indian and Chinese. They also have Mangalorean dishes on the menu which are a must try. They have a nice bar with a wide variety of drinks to choose from.
The ambience is nice with dim lights and a wall full of quotes. The seating is comfortable. The overall look and feel is like a family restaurant and bar. The service was prompt to start with Mahesh taking down the orders. However they took a reasonable amount of time to get all the dishes.

The mocktails we had were Cinderella and Berry Blast. Both these were juice based drinks. Berry blast has Cranberry and Apple juice with a touch of honey.
Cindrella has orange juice and fresh lime which makes it very refreshing.

The food we had was all very good in terms of quality and quantity. I would rate it a value for money place.

We had Murg Toorki which was Chicken Tikka marinated with Cheese and this was delicious. The chicken was cooked to perfection, juicy and charred perfectly. This tasted even better with the mint coriander chutney.

Coriander Chicken Dry was a Chinese appetizer, this was again very good. Herbaceous flavour with garlic and spring onions. Again well cooked Chicken. Very satisfying.

For the main course we had Chicken Ghee Roast with Neer Dosa. My favourite and everything was perfect. Must have when here. Highly recommended.

The Cheese Garlic Naan here is not the usual Naan with the Garlic and Cheese outside. Here it's stuffed inside and is very wholesome.
We had Chicken Betabi which is a red gravy similar to Butter Chicken in many ways with shredded chicken in a luscious velvety gravy.

For dessert we had a sizzling walnut brownie with ice cream. This was fresh and well made.

This place even has outdoor seating which is accessible only post rains. I am totally in awe of the simplicity and the no nonsense kind of approach to serving good quality food.

I am totally coming back here again with my gang for a great meal.

We should have be warned right after entering: no friendly hello from the staff and worst 90s pop songs played way too lout from a DJ (btw: who needs a DJ for that most mainstream unpersonal song selection?).

The interior design is kind of post modern Art Deco but far from being cozy or cool.
*But now for the drinks.*:
One of the reviewers praised them for the story that would be behind each of the signature drinks.
Well, the bar menu mentions a story for each signature drink. But there is no recognisable connection between the story and the drink.
And there is not even necessarily a connection between drink description and drink. Or would you expect a garden salad with plenty of cucumber seeds that fills one third of your glass when only white rum, vodka, lime and syrup are mentioned in the menu? And
One could overlook this, if the two signature drinks we had, would have convinced by creativity and taste. But they didn’t, not at all.
The best signature drinks become classics some day. A good signature drink makes you remember drink and location. These unbalanced drinks we won’t remember.

- The vendor (Sanjay)  was very pro active with us, till the payment went to him. Post that, everything was a blunder.
- Of course in our post event feedback we mentioned all of this to the owner. A few days later the said vendor called us on our honeymoon, and had the audacity to say "Aap mera naam kharab kar rahe ho, maine aapko apna best DJ diya tha" :/

So overall, i would say this place is lovely, in terms of the food, venue and decor. The plush blue sofas promise to provide a cosy seating and the complimentary opener -- the sweet and tangy Papaya strips -- is a tempting way to start the proceedings. The masala peanuts -- which come along with those papaya strips -- might find themselves on the eight ball; replacing them with flavoured cashews might just buttress the unfolding and make it impeccable. Ah, that might be a high expectation!\\n\\nI ordered a watermelon mojito and an orange mojito in mocktails; both were fantastic, came within 10 minutes and had more than average sizes when compared to same-star restaurants. As per instructions, both had medium-power soda and were slightly sweet and sour, respectively. In the appetizers, we ordered a Pork Bao, which is available in two sizes -- small and large ( having two and four pieces, respectively ). We were inside the restaurant well beyond the closing hours and kudos to the staff for ensuring that the experience wasn't compromised.\\n\\nThe hot air balloon emitting dim yellow light is plain looking yet presents a nice aura to sit under for a premium late-night dinner; the richly coloured brown walls deserve a painting or two on them, as is generally the case in such restaurants. The management should aeriously think about renovating the place, name_person=Ajay Bhat}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 years ago, review=I've heard about Chulha a lot and been recommended about the same a lot in the last couple of years so I finally decided to give it a visit on my Dad's birthday this year.

The place is quite fancy given the view you get from the 14th Floor. We chose a place near the window and found it extravagant to sit there and enjoy our food.
(Sadly the seats are really uncomfortable. Maybe its a psychological hack that they just don't want the people to enjoy the view endlessly.)

We ordered Chicken Manchow Soup. The soup was quite tasty and not overloaded with garlic which some restaurants do. But sadly the fried noodles were sour. Which I understand was due to the noodles which had turned stale and then they were fried to avoid wastage.

We asked for recommendations from our server and he recommended Banjara Kebab and Dilkhush kebab. But we had already tried those umpteen times in other restaurants so we rather went for Murgh Maharaja Kebab. It was Chicken Tikka Kebab which was in turn wrapped with Chicken Seekh Kebab. We found the description quite fancy and ordered that. Were served 6 pieces of it. Honestly taste was great but wasn't really value for money. And was on the drier side so had to compensate with the green Chutney and lemon.

Then we ordered Java Style Chicken Lollipop which was really tasty. Though there was no hint of Thai flavor in it. It simply felt it was tossed in Schezwan Sauce.

We then saw Sizzlers on the menu and were really tempted to order the same. So we ordered a Chilli Basil Chicken Sizzler. The quantity was humongous. We were three people and initially I thought only 2 would be able to share but the portion size was more than enough for 3 people. Noodles were sadly soggy and overboiled and sauce was a bit bland for my palette. But it didn't matter much it was tasty.

I ordered a Chicken Tikka Biryani and again the portion size was more than enough for 2 people.

Our total bill was around 2200. And I feel it was all in all a good experience.

Only downside being the server being a bit too smart. While the food is still lovely, the service has gone completely downhill. The staff today seemed disinterested, unresponsive, and worst of all, the manager (who they said is named Raju) was shockingly arrogant, easily one of the most unpleasant interactions I’ve ever had at a restaurant.

Overall, Phulkari by Copper Chimney feels like a cultural celebration on a plate through flavor, color, and creativity., name_person=Aditi Prabhu}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,000–1,200, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Visited July 16, 2025 – day 13 in India

This is another excellent recommendation by my friend Shakun. We are staying at Novotel in Juhu, so we enjoyed a leisurely walk on the beach to reach the restaurant. We were welcomed very graciously and seated by the hostess. Since we had walked on the beach and were all very sandy, my husband, my daughters (aged 5 and 7), and I went to the restroom to wash up. When we returned to our table, I was pleasantly surprised to find it set up with a kids’ menu featuring lots of activities, along with sets of crayons and a chef hat crown that both my girls promptly put on. This was such a refreshing change on our 13th day in India, as until now we hadn’t seen a kids menu specifically geared for children in any of the restaurants we’ve visited. It was definitely a highlight for me.

We were kindly greeted by our servers Mukul and Manojit Roy, and their service throughout our meal was outstanding. They offered thoughtful recommendations, anticipated our needs, checked in at just the right moments without being intrusive, and treated our whole family with genuine warmth and respect.

For dinner, both my daughters wanted popcorn chicken—actually their favorite back home—and they were thrilled to see it on the menu. One chose a vanilla milkshake and the other a chocolate milkshake. The popcorn chicken was a bit spicy for their mild palates—but they loved the milkshakes.

My husband and I chose the Fish and Mixed Meats kebab platter. Mukul honestly informed us that the fish was unavailable, and substituted another chicken kebab, which we were completely fine with. We ordered the kebabs as served, thinking our girls might want to try them—and it turned out to be an excellent decision. The girls devoured the chicken reshmi kebab. It was so satisfying to see them enjoying something from the Indian menu, knowing we’ve found another safe and delicious option for them here in India.

We also ordered Rawalpindi Gosht, extra spicy, along with roomali roti and rice to accompany our meal. My husband was delighted with the kebabs—every bite was melt‑in‑your‑mouth tender. The Rawalpindi Gosht was succulent and richly flavored; we absolutely loved it. Despite being full, Mukul suggested the baked motichoor rabri for dessert. It was absolutely delicious—the warm, layered sweetness with the motichoor bits and creamy rabri was the perfect end to our meal.

We loved everything about this place. From the walk-in welcome to the thoughtful touches for our kids, the exceptional service by Mukul and Manojit, and the outstanding food, Copper Chimney Juhu made our evening truly memorable. The bistro makes you feel in your element with their camaraderie. The atmosphere of this place and the crew connive to make the customer feel like a huésped as they embrace them to their ménage.

The service was pretty good. Our table was hosted by Mr. Rahul, Mr. Nikhil and Mr. Vishal. They helped us out in selecting the dishes and were very friendly. The restaurant being an part of The Empresa, has to manage the hotel guests along with the adventurous diners who visit the place. So it may take a while to get what you order but the food is totally worth the wait.

They serve a variety of dishes from the Mediterranean and North Indian Cuisine. The menu is pretty elaborate and covers a lot of palatable dishes with top class presentation. The chefs collude to serve appetizing and innovative dishes to appease the diners and bring a smile of satisfaction on their faces.

Our table was festooned with salads, burgers, appetizers, risotto and desserts.
We started off with 'Feta & Co. '. It's a salad constructed with the Greek Feta and a combination of fresh fruits and mixed greens. The salty and tangy taste of Feta combined with the flavours of fresh fruits and avocado makes it one of the finest salads in the menu.

The 'Supreme Crisp Burger' had the perfect cohesiveness between the amount of bun, meat and toppings. It was a merger of the chicken supreme patty, onion rings with the side of potato wedges. The bun was nicely toasted to hold up the patty. The quality of the meat used was top class which made the burger very juicy.
We also had 'Easy green Burger' which was served with a side of potato wedges and salads. It had a delectable taste.

We had a few beverages here: 'Passion Fruit Chilli Lemonade' and 'Blueberry & Basil lemonade'. They were very refreshing. The passion fruit chilli tasted really good. It had a spicy twist to it.

reviews:
["{guided_block={}, time_line=Edited 7 years ago, review=Sofitel Wine Days are back! This is held on a monthly basis at The Sofitel Mumbai BKC and I was lucky to be a part of one at Le Bar Diamantaire, located at lobbey level next to Pondicherry Cafe!

A sit down multi course Italian meal with Italian wine is what you witness! An experience unparalleled. Sofitel has always been my one of the most favourite places in Mumbai because of the numerous festivals they do. But the food tried at this event was one of the best that I have ever had!

Every course had its own wine, started with couple of white and finishing with couple of red! All the wines had been specially curated and imported and the food also complemented really well. You have Veg as well as Non Veg options, so one can choose accordingly. Talking about what all I tried at Sofitel Wine Days -

We began with Almond and Goat Cheese as Starters, had Zucchini, Avocado and Mustard Sauce. The non veg equivalent to this was Amaranth Prawns. This was served with the first wine of the evening - Villa Antinori Bianco - white wine. A perfect way to begin your meal! The wine aims at maximizing the Tuscan character of the wine and is straw yellow in colour with greenish highlights. It is still wine with approx 12% alcohol by volume.

Next in line we tried the Forest Mushroom Veloute which was Truffle Mousse, Pine nuts and brioche. Absolutely awesome and I loved the taste! Texture was thick and rich in flavour and aroma. This was served with the second white wine of the evening - Antinori Santa Cristina Pinot Grigio. The wine is straw yellow in colour, the wine offers fruity and delicate aromas of pineapple, green apples and lemon. The wine is refreshing and has approx 12% alcohol by volume.

Moving to the mains - we first had the Baked Courgette which was Duxelle, Edamame and Parmesan Risotto! Again an awesome dish for Mushroom lovers. This was served along with the first red wine of the evening - Antinori Santa Cristina Toscana. For non vegetarians there was Grilled Seabass (Risotto). Wine is a red wine from Toscana, Italy and has approx 12.5% alcohol by volume.

Next main dish was Grilled Polenta which had red lentil ragout, charred leek, fondant potato and caramlised onion straw! A filling dish and really good! I preferred Polenta more than Baked Courgette! This one was served along with Antinori Peppoli Chianti Classico, the last wine / 2nd red wine of the evening. Non veg equivalent was Braised Lamb Shank with same ingredients. The wine represents the Chianti Classico territory and it's historic grape variety with typical floral and fruity aromas. Wine has approx 13% alcohol by volume.

We ended our meal with one of the most amazing desserts - Berry Trail. It had Raspberry Parfait, Blueberry Jelly, Blackberry Chantilly, Oats Crumble and Berry Chocolate Crisps. One of the best dessert that I have had till date! Simply awesome.

In complete awe of the experience at Sofitel Mumbai BKC! As mentioned earlier, they keep doing #sofitelwinedays often, almost every month and I would highly recommend everyone including all wine connoisseurs!, name_person=Jatin Shah}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=7 years ago, review=Sofitel BKC  has been our favourite hub to enjoy some family times , thanks to their Festivals which they organise with great enthusiasm .

To begin with, the vegetarian selection was extremely limited, which itself was disappointing for a premium luxury hotel. What made it worse was that several items had already run out by around 9:30–10 PM, which is surprisingly early for a dinner buffet. The veg sushi, in particular, was tucked away inside the refrigerator with no proper labelling or indication—it genuinely felt like a game of hide-and-seek unless you already knew where to look.

Overall, this dinner experience was a 5/10 at best. I recently visited Pondicherry Café at Sofitel in Mumbai, and unfortunately, the experience fell far below expectations. Here’s a detailed breakdown of my visit:

Parking Hassle

As someone who arrived on a motorbike, the experience began with a significant disappointment. The hotel does not provide motorbike parking within its premises. Instead, I was directed to a pay-and-park lot 300 meters away, located on an open ground opposite Jio International School. This parking area was poorly maintained and inconvenient, especially for those with huge bikes like mine. I had to leave my bike without a handle locked, which was unsettling.

Walking from the parking lot to the hotel in the scorching sun further diminished the experience. For a luxury hotel, this lack of accommodation for bikers is surprising and disheartening.

Ambience and Atmosphere

Once inside, the ambience of Pondicherry Café was pleasant but lacked any accompanying music, which made it feel somewhat lifeless. The décor was appealing, but the overall atmosphere could use some warmth and vibrance to match the expectations of a premium dining experience.

Buffet Experience

We opted for the buffet based on its promising menu, but the food did not deliver in terms of taste. While there was a variety of options available, very few stood out. Here’s a breakdown of the meal:
•	Soup: 2/5 – Bland and unremarkable.
•	Starters: 3/5 – Only two items were decent; the rest were forgettable.
•	Main Course: 2/5 – A disappointing selection with subpar flavors.
•	Desserts: 2/5 – Average at best. The pista kulfi had an odd paan flavor, which didn’t appeal to me.
•	Pizza & Pasta: Possibly the worst I’ve ever had.

Overall, the food lacked flavor and quality, especially considering the premium pricing.

Service

The service was another letdown. Staff were hard to find when needed, whether it was for cutlery or water. This lack of attentiveness added to the frustration and further detracted from the overall dining experience.

Final Thoughts

For a restaurant within a luxury hotel, Pondicherry Café failed to meet expectations on multiple fronts. The motorbike parking issue, coupled with an underwhelming dining experience, made this visit quite disappointing. Considering the high ratings this restaurant holds on platforms like Zomato and Google, I feel it is overrated.

Recommendation:
•	For Bikers: Avoid this place if you value convenience and proper parking facilities.
•	For Food Lovers: There are far better dining options in the BKC area offering superior taste, service, and overall experience at similar or lower price points.

Overall Rating:
•	Ambience: 3/5
•	Food Taste: 2/5
•	Service: 2/5
•	Value for Money: 1/5

The portion size was good, the flavours were balanced, and everything was served hot and well-prepared. It’s the kind of comfort food Chili’s is known for, and it didn’t disappoint.

While I fully support tipping for good service, adding it automatically and at a relatively high percentage didn’t feel right — especially considering the level of service we received. The service wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t exceptional enough to justify a mandatory 10% charge. Tips should always feel voluntary and earned, not forced.

The ambience also felt different compared to the older Chili’s outlets. This place gives of a little bit futuristic neon vibes with pink and light blue colours dominating the decor. With the bar on one end and tables across the floor this place is as good as it gets.

They even host live music every now and then, please check with the lounge before visiting. Their drinks section is quite huge with a menu as extensive as it can be. There’s a liquor or cocktail for everyone!

The service is also super fast, staff is very courteous and helpful in guiding through the menu. The dish presentation is also quite neat. Our food was on the table within a few minutes of ordering.

Coming to the food we had a few cocktails and a few veg and non veg starters. The cocktails were really good, they were strong punchy and had a good flavour. Apparently, it was. Instead of simply pouring the measured wine back, the bartender (Bhavesh) decided to keep the extra wine for himself and snapped, “You wanted the standard serving - this is it.”

But despite the charming name and the promise of a thoughtfully curated Italian menu, the experience left more to be desired than remembered.

The meal started on a reasonably positive note. The Spaghetti Carbonara arrived with a creamy, well-emulsified sauce that clung nicely to the strands of pasta. The presence of pork gave the dish some much-needed body and savouriness, though it was hard to tell if guanciale was used. The overall flavour was pleasant, if unremarkable, and the dish did what it needed to without dazzling.

Unfortunately, the meal only declined from there.

The Steak, requested medium rare, did arrive at the correct doneness, which deserves acknowledgement. But that’s where the positives end. The cut of meat itself was a poor choice—tough, chewy, and devoid of the tenderness one expects from a properly sourced and rested steak. For a dish that typically commands a premium on any menu, this one felt more like an afterthought than a main event.

The Salmon Bruschetta fared no better. Topped with pallid, clearly farmed salmon that lacked freshness, the dish suffered from a lack of depth and definition. The cream which is meant to support or complement actually ended up dominating the plate. The result was a bland, vaguely fishy bite that could have come from any cold appetiser counter rather than a kitchen claiming Italian sophistication.

And therein lies the central issue with Napoli by Shatranj. While it gestures toward authenticity and finesse, the food rarely lands with the kind of precision or character that might distinguish it. The pricing, meanwhile, reflects a confidence that the food does not back up. At best, it feels like another stylish Bandra restaurant with a name borrowed from Naples but very little of its soul.

The level 2 dining area is a proper bar set up as it is  dim and looks amazing. My personal favourite one would be the rooftop which looks absolutely stunning and a perfect one for the date nights.

The F&B spread over here is exceptionally amazing. On bar they have brewed beers so all the beer fanatics you guys are covered too. In drinks we had Gin Botanic which was basically cucumber G&T which was super refreshing and had lovely taste. Next we had double trouble which was mix of cranberry juice topped with 2 shot glasses having whiskey and Jäegermeister each. This was my personal favourite and a must try if you are here. For the starters we tried Thecha Chicken Kebab which was perfectly tandoor-ed inside out and the kick from green chillies was quite dominant. Next we had Prawns in black pepper sauce. Upon our server’s recommendation we also tried chicken pepper dimsums which was really good too. Paper thin outer layer and generously filled with juicy chicken filling this was lovely. Our meal ended with their Ghee roast chicken pizza which was made using thin crust and loaded with toppings. The traditional flavours of ghee roast on to a pizza was super delicious and one of the best fusion pizzas we have tried off late.

Location & ambience
•	Gallops is located inside the Mahalaxmi Race Course in Mumbai, which gives it a uniquely lush, open-green backdrop uncommon in the city’s dining scene.  ￼
•	The décor and setting combine colonial charm with upscale comfort: for example, walnut-floors, candle-light chandeliers, and equestrian-themed décor post-revamp.  ￼
•	Outdoor and al-fresco dining is one of its strong suits — especially nice in cooler months.  ￼

2. Food quality & menu variety
•	The menu successfully blends Indian and Continental dishes. From traditional kebabs and curries to refined European-style mains, there’s something for varied tastes.  ￼
•	Signature dishes that get strong mentions:
•	“Dori Kebab” (mutton or chicken) – minced, skewered and charcoal-cooked.  ￼
•	“Chicken Ala Kiev” with cheese/butter-filled centre, as a refined European choice.  ￼
•	Desserts are also strong: Baked Alaska and newer additions like Baileys Caramel Cloud.  ￼
•	Many reviewers emphasize the generous portions, good presentation and a sense of value for a fine-dining venue.  ￼

3. Service & experience
•	The service is frequently praised: attentive staff, good recommendations (e.g., for wine or pairings), smooth reservation experience when booked in advance.  ￼
•	The overall dining experience is described as memorable— especially when everything aligns (good table, nice view, well-timed service). For example:
“What a wonderful restaurant from the minute we arrived the staff were so efficient and helpful, the food was absolutely incredible.”  ￼

4. Ideal for special occasions / date nights
•	The ambience, décor and location make it ideal for anniversaries, special dinners or when you want to treat yourself. Many mentions of formative visits, nostalgic moments, photo-friendly setting.  ￼

If I were picking one restaurant for a refined Mumbai meal — especially if you’re after something more than just dinner but an experience — Gallops checks a lot of boxes:
•	A setting that feels premium yet relaxed.
•	A menu that offers both familiar Indian comfort and elevated Continental touches.
•	Good enough service to let you focus on the evening rather than logistics.
•	A chance to dine in one of Mumbai’s less-hustle zones (given the race-course setting) while still being accessible.

An iconic Mumbai café with a lively vibe and historic charm. Great place to relax after Colaba Causeway shopping—food is decent, drinks are good, and the atmosphere is the real highlight.

Leopold Cafe is worth visiting for its history and energetic ambience. The food is average for the price, but the experience, crowd, and location make it a must-visit spot in South Mumbai.

Very vibrant and famous place with lots of character. Can be crowded and slightly overpriced, but still worth a visit at least once for the iconic Mumbai café experience.

📍 About the Place
Leopold Cafe is one of Mumbai’s oldest and most famous cafés, founded in 1871 and located on Colaba Causeway — right across from the Colaba Police Station. It’s a cultural landmark as well as a popular hangout for tourists, locals, and fans of the novel Shantaram.

The café also carries historical significance because it was one of the spots attacked during the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, and some bullet marks remain preserved as a memorial.

🍽️ Ambience & Atmosphere
Vibe:
Lively, bustling, and full of character — a bit of an old-school vibe with a mix of retro and bohemian decor.

Great people-watching spot after a shopping stroll along Colaba Causeway.

Often packed, especially in evenings and weekends — queues are common

🍔 Food & Drinks — What People Say
Positives:
Wide, varied menu with continental, Indian, Chinese & bar food options.

Popular items include beer towers, shepherd’s pie, walnut pie, chocolate desserts, chicken wings, burgers and more.

Some reviewers have enjoyed refreshing drinks like Coke floats and milkshakes.

Cost:
Expect mid-range pricing — around ₹2500 for two people including drinks (approx.) with alcohol.

🧑‍🍳 Service & Crowd
What reviewers note:
✔ Friendly, helpful staff when it’s not crowded.
⚠ Can be slow or inattentive during peak hours.
⚠ Busy weekends and evenings often have lines and waiting times.

📌 Pro Tips Before You Go
This cafe is worth visiting for the experience and atmosphere, even if the food opinions vary.

Best to visit earlier in the day or on weekdays to avoid long waits.

Located right on SV Road

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=Having lived and worked in Japan, albeit many moons ago, I was not expecting to be reminded of the tastes and feel of a typical izakaya in the land of the rising sun, in, of all places, Bandra, Mumbai.
We were ushered to our seating by a raucous welcome from the Kuuraku staff, which was more reminiscent of the Wankhede Stadium than a Japanese restaurant. But there was a effervescence about the staff at Kuuraku, reflecting the confidence that they have in their excellent food.
We ordered the Special Kushi Course, comprising 5 sticks of yakitori. The standout of this was the chicken tail. It was so good that we ordered two extra sticks of this, named bonjiri shio. We also ordered a portion of pork belly yakitori although this was very slightly disappointing as it was a little on the tough side. Another slight disappointment was the chargrilled asparagus wrapped in pork belly. Again, the pork belly wasn't as tender as I expected and the asparagus was a little small and fibrous. However, the edamame challenge was a lot of fun. The idea is to grab as much edamame as possible with one hand - and what you grab is what you get to eat. I used my goalkeeper hands to grab, what the server told me was an over par amount. The edamame was quite good too. The crunchy ebi roll was very generous too coming as a generous portion. The temperature of the rice was spot on as was the consistency. Could the quality of the rice be higher as in Japan? Well yes if you can get that rice but otherwise it really was excellent. The same goes for the pork rice. Here the consistency or the stickiness of the rice was more important than in the ebi roll and if they could get better rice it was be amazing. The slight disappointment was the inclusion of bell peppers. Heresy! Finally, the tea was served in a beautiful black pot, again, very true to Japan.
All in all this was an excellent place with a really true feel of Japan, helped also by the constant stream of Japanese music and the service was particularly excellent. The ambience is classy and modern, with dim lighting and elegant décor that sets the mood right away. Service is top-notch—staff are attentive without being pushy, and they explain each dish like it’s part of a story.

The food is creative Indian cuisine with a fine-dining twist. Presentation is Instagram-worthy, and the flavors are balanced, though sometimes you feel it’s more about style than portion size. The tasting menu is fun if you want to try a bit of everything, but be prepared—it’s not cheap.

Cocktails are inventive, with unique flavors and presentation that match the restaurant’s vibe. Dessert was the highlight for me—beautifully plated and actually tasted as good as it looked.

The only downside is the price. This is definitely a special-occasion place, not somewhere you drop in for a casual dinner. Also, if you prefer classic, straightforward Indian food, the fusion style here may not be your thing.

The menu is classic, inspired from 200 year old recipes which were cooked in the royal kitchens of Awadh under the rulership of Nawabs. This has been extensively researched by the ITC Master Chefs when they were opening the original Dum Pukht at ITC Maurya and it’s clearly evident in the taste. The Dum Pukht here in mumbai is excellent since Imitiaz Qureshi Ji had shifted to this branch and all the favourites were and are to date faithfully rendered. Current head chef Asif Qureshi Ji is also an excellent chef giving out great dishes consistently. The melt in mouth Kakori Kebab is out of this world, something that has the potential to stay on your palette for years, beautifully seasoned and cooked to perfection it’s a perfect representation of a kebab. The dining room also needs a revamp I guess considering the interiors of other Dum Pukht branches. Rest, I think it’s perfection. Service is also amazing, shoutout to Priya for making my lunch worthwhile. Starters That Set the Bar High:
The Stuffed Cheese Chicken Tikka was an absolute crowd-pleaser. Juicy, smoky chicken with a gooey cheese center — what’s not to love? Each bite was flavorful and perfectly spiced. A fusion twist came in the form of the Mutton Boti Bhel — a creative take that combined tender chunks of spiced mutton with the crunch of bhel puri. It was spicy, tangy, and addictive, offering a street-style zing with gourmet quality.

Mains That Sizzle and Satisfy:
If you love sizzlers, don’t miss their Peri Peri Chicken Sizzler. Served piping hot and still crackling, the chicken was coated in a fiery peri peri marinade, resting on a bed of herbed rice and grilled veggies. It delivered on both spice and satisfaction. For something more traditional, the Kala Mutton is a must. Rich, deeply spiced, and slow-cooked to perfection, this Maharashtrian-style curry is hearty and hits all the right notes for mutton lovers.

A Sweet Finish:
Ending on a sweet note, the Gulab Jamun Donuts were as indulgent as they sound. Think soft donuts soaked in classic gulab jamun syrup — a fusion dessert that manages to celebrate the best of both worlds. We had a table reservation for 9:45 PM and arrived by 9:55 PM. Despite being just 10 minutes late, we were made to wait another 10 minutes before being seated—even though we could clearly see 4–5 empty tables inside. This initial delay set the tone for what turned out to be an underwhelming evening.

Once seated, we weren’t provided with menus until we asked for them. After deciding on our soups and starters, no server approached us for over 10 minutes, prompting me to personally request someone to take our order. There was no water on the table, and even after requesting it, the server simply forgot—walking past our table multiple times to serve others. Eventually, I had to approach someone who seemed to be the manager, only to be told, repeatedly, that “the staff is busy” and we needed to “co-operate.” Frankly, it doesn’t take much effort to bring menus, take an order, or serve water—basic expectations at any restaurant.

As for the food:

Soups: The Manchow soup was lukewarm and seemed like it came straight from the buffet, with soggy fried noodles on the side. The Tomato soup, on the other hand, had a nice basil flavor and was decent.

Starters: The Paneer Chilly was flavorful and enjoyable. Among the non-veg options, the Korean Fried Chicken had an odd fishy smell, although the sauce was good. The Pan Fried Chicken Momos were tasty, though the accompanying dip was overly sweet.

Main Course: The Chicken Tikka Masala and assorted breads were well-prepared and satisfying. However, the Chicken Biryani was disappointing—bland and lacking any real depth of flavor. The vegetarian mains—Vegetable Stir Fry in Hot Garlic Sauce and Pink Pasta—were good but took an unusually long time to arrive.

Mocktails: We tried the No-jito, a twist on the classic mojito, which didn’t stand out, and the Guava Mary, which was refreshing and enjoyable.

No desserts were ordered, mainly because by the end of the meal, our patience was running thin.

Overall, the dining experience was marred by disorganized service, inattentive staff, and inconsistent food quality. While a few dishes did manage to impress, they weren’t enough to outweigh the frustrating delays and lack of basic hospitality. For a restaurant that seems to take pride in its offerings, the service fell severely short.

Cafe Trofima, located near the bustling Shivaji Park in Dadar, has garnered attention as a popular hangout spot, but it falls short of the hype for several reasons.

Food

The menu boasts a variety of food options, including breakfast platters, which might initially seem impressive. However, the taste of the food is compromised and does not justify the high prices. For a cafe that markets itself as a premium experience, the quality of the dishes leaves much to be desired.

Ambience and Seating

The sitting space is one of the better aspects of Cafe Trofima. Considering it is a cafe, the seating is comfortable and suitable for casual conversations or work. However, the overall ambience is just average, with no music to elevate the vibe. It lacks the warmth or charm that many would expect from a cafe in this area.

Service

The service is satisfactory but nothing extraordinary. While the staff is polite and attends to customers in a timely manner, the overall experience doesn’t stand out as memorable.

Location and Accessibility

A significant downside is the lack of parking space, which can be a hassle, especially given the busy location of Shivaji Park. Visitors arriving in their own vehicles may find it inconvenient.

Pricing

The prices are on the higher side, making it hard to justify for the quality of food and overall experience provided. While there are plenty of food options to choose from, the value for money is not reflected in the offerings.

Verdict

Cafe Trofima is overrated and doesn’t quite live up to its reputation. While it has some redeeming qualities like decent seating and satisfactory service, the compromised food taste, lack of parking, and high prices make it hard to recommend wholeheartedly. It could work as a one-time visit for those curious about its breakfast platters, but better options are available in and around the area for a more satisfying experience.

Orchid can be easily said to be one of the best ecotel hotel since years. Buffet of them had really lot of options. View from the restaurant is excellent too. Certainly a must visit restaurant if you want to enjoy the lavish spread. Strongly recommend, go for it.

Location- This restaurant is on the first floor of very famous ecotel hotel Orchid. Orchid is just adjacent to the domestic airport.(5/5)

Theme- Being the main restaurant of the hotel it's 24*7, it serves mix cuisine with a la carte and buffet both.(5/5)

Ambience- one side of first floor is occupied by this restaurant so yes it's really big. Divided into small sections. You can get a lobby view from any table.  One side of restaurant they got lovely spreaded buffet . Lighting is bright n fresh. Got mix tables or 2,4,8 covers. Soft music at background was nice.(5/5)

Food- This being a main restaurant of the hotel, it is open 24*7. You either can go for a la carte menu or decide to go with the lavish buffet spread. We decided to hog on buffet which looked really impressive.  Buffet consist of soup, salads, farsaan,starters, Chaat counter, main courses, desserts.(5/5)

Soup was the first dish I tastes and was highly impressive with the taste of it. It was seafood clear soup which was made with fish stock, fish chunks, thick sliced celery. Great way to start.
Chaat counter had various options like seven Puri, dahi Puri, dahi wada, bhel. You have to order your dish to the chef who was standing on the counter and he will send it to your table.
I had a go at dahi Puri which was delicious.

Starters they had paneer Tikka, corn bruschetta, fish fingers, chicken in Asian style. Fish finger was the dish I kept eating for long, fresh fish and crispy enough.

Salad counter had mix of veg and nonveg salads, loved the smoked salmon salad and tuna potato salad.
Very rare that I saw a farsaan options in multicuisine restaurant of 5*. They were serving bakerwadi and khokla, I didn't try it though was looking tempting.
Same section had options of nachos with in-house cheese sauce.

Main course really had many options. Pasta  live counter seemed very busy. I opted for more Indian food as awadhi gosht korma caught my attention. Excellent colour with medium thickness gravy and well cooked lamb in it was heaven with the butter naan (any bread options you like) which they serve on table.
Dishes like Pan seared fish with garlic cilantro butter sauce, chicken in black bean sauce were a must try.
Coming to rice , I saw Chicken biryani  first time itself when was checking the buffet. So took biryani with some for a gravy. Biryani was well made with long grain rice, garnished well with fried onions and had extraordinary aroma of it's own, Enjoyed it.

Dessert section is always said to be the best part of any buffet, it's true. Here they had mix if Indian and continental desserts. Eddie’s Bistro has long been on my radar, and I finally decided to give their Iftaar menu a whirl, expecting nothing less than a feast for the senses. Right from the get-go, the presentation scored high marks; the food arrived in pristine packaging that promised good things within.

Carnivorous Delights Unleashed:
The evening kicked off with Lamb Sliders, a real treat for the palate. These little delights were packed with tender, juicy lamb that melted in the mouth—clearly the star of the evening. Each bite was a perfect symphony of flavors, making it hard not to crave more.

Vegetarian Surprise:
Next up, the Paneer Chilly. Soft, succulent cubes of paneer tossed in a spicy sauce that had a kick but was incredibly flavorful. It was a bit on the spicy side for my taste, but it seemed to hit the right note with everyone else at the table, proving that spice is indeed the variety of life.

Kebab Corner:
The Chicken Seekh Kebab lived up to its reputation. Perfectly cooked with spices that sang through each bite, it was a testament to the careful preparation and love that went into its creation. It’s always a pleasure when a dish meets your high expectations, and these kebabs did just that.

A Chinese Twist:

Different members of the kitchen team explained each dish in detail. The team was very passionate and sweet. They also invited us to tour the kitchen and offered my parents a small token for their anniversary. :)

The tasting menu experience easily takes two hours and we are very grateful for the innovative dishes and the hard work behind it.

I am sharing in the pictures a few of the dishes and the menu we ate (the pictures are mostly in order).

In terms of favorities: we really loved the main dishes with the mushroom risotto and sheet pasta with chickpea cutlet. Not to mention the bite size starters were extremely exiting! At no point did we feel the food was too much or not enough. Despite being a 20 course tasting menu it was just right!

We weren't completely in love with the sweets, but maybe that's more on us not having much of a sweet tooth.

Small note: we usually don't have leafs that are already eaten by worms. Despite being heavily processed there is always a chance that their is egg residue left behind. One of the leaf dishes did have such leafs. On us pointing it out the chef mentioned that its processed very well after coming from the farm. I would have personally prefered having dishes without them. But understand if that's a choice restaurant makes to keep them in., name_person=Tanvi Goyal}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=4 weeks ago, review=An appreciation message for one of the girls during lunch service- I don’t remember who it was but - my friend who works with leaves and textile design took the skeleton leaf garnish from my cocktail. She’d put it on the table waiting for it to dry. This girl noticed and came along with a box of tissues so that my friend could carefully put the leaf between paper and keep it safe and dry.

All of us at the table noticed it but somehow while leaving we forgot to mention it and show our appreciation for her.

But I this is what sets apart the best restaurants from the good ones. It’s not just food, which Ekaa is obviously excellent at, but it is this attention to detail that keeps us coming back. This is what makes Ekaa Ekaa., name_person=Anshul Shah}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=The place itself has a chill vibe, super friendly staff, and great music.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Good ambience , good service, good food , fine classy taste..}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=We got 5 tapas, 5 mains and 2 desserts + cocktails between 5 people.}"]

The popular chef has left, and so have the quality & standards ...

A dinner on a fine day at this premium property was not destined to go well. Romano's, a restaurant which I had visited twice before, known for its close to flawless service & dishes, typical Italian style preparation and cuisine, and not to forget the sea bass, which was the best ever I had eaten anywhere in the same level hotels, but now it was all history. Today, the same restaurant had a below-average experience in stock for me.

Dishes took longer than the expected time. I had ordered a salmon and a sea bass and was told that it would take 20 and 25 mins respectively, but it took quite longer than that. While the salmon had a flaw, which upon complaining was first met with a response that it was good according to them, but they eventually agreed to replace it. Needless to say, taste buds do differ. Even on the second count, it didn't taste as it normally does. Surely not the first time I have tried it, and in fact, I have tried it in the same property a few times, and it was delicious previously, but this time, no offence intended, tasted weird. The quantity was too small, perhaps the smallest salmon I have eaten hitherto. This is highly likely because of the food festival discount which the restaurant offered. The second dish sea bass was not as good as last time, but still good enough. Again, the portion was quite small. The preparation was also different compared to last time.

The bread basket which is otherwise served, wasn't in this case ( I saw other customers getting one ). Again, this could be because I was availing a food festival offer. Even the mocktails took over 15 mins to be served, which is surprising, and instructions of less ice weren't followed. The blue mocktail was on a mild sweet and tangy side, and tasted good. The yellow one was average. The quantity of mocktails was medium. The restaurant was not too crowded either, so the wait time is indeed surprising.

Contrary to the case in the same level hotels, no one came to check in how the dishes were, and it was not easy to call the servers. The servers took a long time to come, and even when complained to someone in the coat ( I assume, a supervisor ), I was told sorry, but nothing changed. The supervisor didn't look much concerned about the experience and never came back to check if the concerns were resolved or not.

Attempts to resolve the concern at a senior level later ( since they weren't resolved in the restaurant properly ) went in vain. I was told that the issue would be looked into. However, my further messages were met with no response, which talks loudly about how much the senior level cares for the customers.

I wouldn't feel like going here again given their overall remiss approach. This wasn't even a four-star service. Christian Moreau Chablis 2016

It is very rare to find a Christian Moreau Chablis in India, and it was nice to see this wine on the menu at Le Cirque, Mumbai, and I ordered the same for my dinner.

Christian Moreau is one of the oldest and most respected domains in Chablis.
Wine has fruit notes like apple, green apple, pear etc.
A very beautiful and amazing Chablis wine.

Food Review:
A great wine needs great food.
That’s where the restaurant failed badly, and food was below average.

Initially their regular Chef prepared a dish based on lobster, and probably lobster was stale and the food was very bad which is not expected from such a restaurant.
Next a prawn based dish which was completely bad as well.
Finally I had a discussion with the restaurant manager and has concluded to change the regular Chef to another Chef Kamlesh to take over the dishes for dinner.
Kamlesh was comparatively better I felt when he prepared further dishes.

To be frank the restaurant had only me as a customer for the whole evening and it was very empty. Only one more customer came for a very short snacks that evening on another table.

I used to be a regular customer of the same restaurant Le Cirque in Bangalore which was much better as per my experience.

Followed by Pomfret dish which was quite average.
Next, another baked fish and vegetables.

Dessert:
The Chef Kamlesh suggested a portion of Crème Brûlée + Tiramisu.
Crème Brûlée was nice and tiramisu was average.

Conclusion:
To conclude, the overall experience was far below expectations.
The restaurant also didn’t had any special dishes like fish roe/caviar or scallops on the menu.
Food menu needs a lot of improvements to include fine dining dishes.
I could see that “Leela” failing very badly on expectations in Mumbai.

A Disappointing Experience – Overrated & Overhyped

If you’re planning a special evening at Liv Eatery & Bar, a rooftop restaurant located in Wagle Estate, Thane, you might want to reconsider. Our recent visit turned out to be the worst dining experience we’ve had in a long time, leaving us frustrated, disappointed, and still hungry.

Location & Ambience: 2/5

Let’s start with the location – while the building itself is new and modern, the area around it is dusty, unhygienic, and gives off a creepy vibe, especially after sunset. Upon arrival, guests are required to check in at the reception to get an entry pass before heading up to the 14th floor via a lift.

As we stepped out onto the rooftop, the Valentine’s Day decoration with red heart-shaped props and crimson focus lights was meant to create a romantic atmosphere. Unfortunately, it felt cheap and borderline eerie, more like a setup from a low-budget horror flick than a cozy date spot.

Seating arrangements were a major letdown.
The tables for couples were tiny, cramped, and paired with uncomfortable chairs. Even the waitstaff admitted that the seating was impractical. They added an extra small table to accommodate our order, but it hardly helped. We spent the evening struggling for space rather than enjoying our time.

Service: 1/5

Right from the moment we sat down, we noticed a pattern – the waitstaff was indifferent, inattentive, and seemed disinterested in serving guests. We had to wave multiple times just to get a menu card, setting the tone for what would be a frustrating dining experience.

Food Quality & Taste: 1/5

We ordered Chicken Cheese Kebabs with Jalapeños. The dish arrived with an “okayish” presentation with 6 pieces, but the taste was only spicy. The chicken inside was flavorless, and we had to request salt separately to make chicken somewhat palatable.

Our second dish was supposed to be a safe bet – Chicken Crispy, a personal favorite of my wife. What arrived was an utter disaster. The chicken was so rubbery and chewy that it felt like chewing gum. After just 2-3 bites, my wife gave up. I pushed myself to eat half the plate, but it left me with jaw pain and frustration. We left the rest of the dish untouched.

Interestingly, the couple seated next to us had also left their food untouched, and at the time, we wondered why. After our ordeal with the Chicken Crispy, we completely understood their decision. Wasting food is never ideal, but when it’s this inedible, it’s the only choice.

Smoky Atmosphere: 2/5

Adding to our misery, the restaurant is a smoker’s paradise. Smoke from nearby tables and bar counters constantly filled the air, making it unpleasant and suffocating for non-smokers like us.
Forget about enjoying your meal – you’ll spend half the time waving away smoke.

Final Straw: We Left Hungry

Frustrated and dissatisfied, we left the place with half-empty stomachs and headed to another restaurant to salvage what was left of our evening. Thankfully, we finally had good food elsewhere, but the damage to our mood was already done.

Overrated & Not Recommended

Liv Eatery & Bar is heavily overrated, and the reality falls far short of the hype. If you value good food, attentive service, and a pleasant atmosphere, this is not the place for you.
Spend your hard-earned money somewhere else where both your taste buds and your mood are respected.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 months ago, review=Hunky Dory is located inside Lemon Tree Premier Malad West and it is easy to find.

The restaurant is spacious with a mini and a full sized bar. The ambiance is super bright with tribal decor touch. Loved the colours used everywhere and every corner looks really beautiful. The seatings are arranged nicely and options for all size of groups are available. They also have DJ section and a dedicated space for live events.

The menu contains global dishes with sone traditional Indian food being available too. Loved the menu as you get everything from sushi to chicken tikka is available in their menu. Prices are at par with similar type of brands and the quantity served is nice. Also they do run dining offers so check online before visiting.

We went here for late lunch and kitchen service was decent but table service was haywire as the staff was super confused as they were booked for a private party at 6PM so I think they were under immense pressure as they kept on switching dishes on different tables. However staff Sandeep tried his best to make the table service smooth.

What We Had -
APPETISERS~
Butter Paneer Potli -
Butter paneer stuffed in a potli, fried to perfection but not oily, and served with a makhani dip. What I liked most was that it wasn’t sweet, the flavors of spices and onions really stood out, making the dish taste perfect.

Herb Crusted Truffle Parmesan Chicken Tikka -
One of the classy version of chicken tikka which tasted amazing. Perfectly grilled juicy chicken done in green spices topped with cheese with light truffle oil and with walnuts on the top tasted perfect. Everything in this tasted superb and you should definitely try this.

Golden Prawn Tempura Roll -
Again one of the best sushi experiences. Their portion is 5 pieces so you will definitely crave more. Crunchy tempura, fresh prawns, spicy sauce and everything in this sushi was perfect.

MAINS~
Wild Mushroom & Truffle Cacio E Pepe -
Man. This was one of the best pasta I have ever had. Earthy flavours due to mushrooms and truffle oil. Perfectly done spaghetti with crunchy veggies and the watery cheese sauce was outstanding. Try it to believe it.

Prawn Ghee Pepper Roast with Tadka Lemon Coriander Rice -
Fresh prawns in ghee roast gravy tasted good. The rice went nicely however I am not a fan of whole coriander hence full marks for gravy.

DESSERT~
Slow Baked Chocolate Bar -
This wasn’t that great as the chocolate used was not that tasty.

MOCKTAILS~
Black & Yellow.
Tropical Delight.
Both the drinks had perfect taste.

So our meal at Hunky Dory Malad was really good. Leaving the service, the food, ambience and music played was perfect. The restaurant arranged a sort of private table for us, which made it feel special and comfortable for our large gathering. The ambiance has a nice rustic charm, and it felt like the perfect place to sit back, enjoy conversations, and share a hearty meal.

We began with soups – some of us chose the Cream of Tomato, while a few went for the Vegetable Manchow. The Cream of Tomato was spot on with its rich yet balanced sweetness, smooth consistency, a drizzle of cream, and crunchy breadcrumbs to top it off. It was satisfying and flavorful. However, the Manchow soup was a bit of a letdown – while it had plenty of veggies, it was extra spicy and lacked that signature tang and flavor one usually expects. Adding fried noodles made it slightly better, but overall it fell short compared to the tomato soup.

The honey chilli potatoes tasted good but were overwhelmingly spicy despite us asking for medium spice. The stuffed mushrooms were generously portioned and very well received – smoky from the tandoor, with a flavorful paneer and veggie filling. On the other hand, the peanut chaat didn’t quite work for us; it had a vinegar-like coating that felt unusual, making the dish more average than enjoyable.

Moving on to the main course, we ordered Malai Kofta, Paneer Butter Masala, and Veg Handi, along with a mix of rotis, naans, and makai roti. The Malai Kofta was outstanding – rich cashew gravy, creamy but not overly sweet, with soft, perfectly cooked koftas that paired wonderfully with the hot rotis. The breads were soft, served hot, and generously buttered – the perfect partner to the gravies.

It might sound cliché, but this is the first time I’m genuinely using the term hidden gem — this place truly surprised me with how good it was in every aspect.

The restaurant is spacious with two different sections being available. One is AC with high chair seatings and a bar plus DJ space too and the other is Non AC causal seatings with pool table in the center and a nice bar. Loved the use of the space and the wall designs as it looked really happening. Currently as IPL is going on they have decorated the Non AC section with team flags and have kept a big screen too.

The menu here is vast and they have options available in Indian, Asian, Italian and some more cuisines. Right now they have added a limited edition mango menu too. Apart from this they have various offers in food and drinks specially for big groups for IPL season. Prices are at par with similar type of brands and the quantity served is good.

Went here on a Monday dinner and the kitchen service was on time and table service by staff Mantu was great as he was polite and knew the menu well.

What We Had -
APPETISERS~
Jamaican Jerk Spice Chicken Tikka -
Served in a unique way as hanging skewers in the Dubai frame. Served with buttery naan, onion and green chutney this was juicy chicken tikkas done in green Jamaican spices. Loved the taste of this as it was not the regular tikka and the spices had nice hint of hotness to it.

Genkai Prawns Maki Roll -
Surprisingly a very nice and tasty sushi served. Fresh prawns rolled nicely with rice and the crunchy tempura coating with spicy sauce tasted excellent. Loved everything about this sushi as it was bang on tasty.

MAINS~
Mushroom & Truffle Cream Cheese Flatbread -
Thin base topped with generous amount of cheese, mushrooms, red chillies, cream cheese and sprayed with aromatic and earthy truffle oil looked perfect and tasted delicious. Loved the juicy mushrooms and the cream cheese and they were honest in using the truffle oil hence a perfect dish again.

Nasi Goreng -
This was a complete miss for me as it was way different from the Nasi Goreng that I have been eating for years. Maybe it is their way as I felt it was a plain normal fried rice however being fried rice it tasted nice but for Nasi Goreng they need to check the recipe.

DESSERT~
Mango Cheesecake -
Again a very different version of cheesecake as this was more closer to a baked layered malai cake with mango flavour and topped with Alphonse mango. Taste wise it was really good as the mango was sweet and it was not extra sweet.

MOCKTAILS~
Tropical Bliss.
Sunset Bloom.
Both the mocktails tasted refreshing as the ingredients tasted nice with each other.

So our meal at What’s Your Plan was really good as the food tasted perfect, the ambiance plus vibe of the restaurant is great and the service was excellent. We came across a newly opened party place in Sakinaka Andheri which looks very promising with great Craft beers, good food and very lively indoor & outdoor section – Perfect for all party people!

We were here on a Monday rainy afternoon, and the mood was just right for some beers & good music!

We tasted their 3 varieties of Craft beers by Barba -  Rize / Moon & Bold and loved all 3 favors! However, I ordered Bold & Moon mugs for our time spent here!

We paired the beers with few lip smacking appetizers such a “House Avocado Toast” which was prepared freshly followed by “Lebanese Platter” which was beautifully presented with 3 different dips, the “Peri Peri Chicken Tikka” had the right amount of spice to flame your tastebuds with the tikkas being well marinated and lastly “Pomfret Tawa Fry” was an absolute delight as well – Wholesome Pomfret in red marination well cooked and served.

For the main course, we opted for “Chettinad Chicken with Malabar Paratha” which had the right spices in play and was bones with good chunks of chicken added; paired well with freshly made flaky malabar paratha

The owner of the place is passionate about food and hospitality and it shows. Guest feedback is well appreciated and this gracious approach instantly makes the place worth visiting again.

On our most recent visit — a Sunday — we were somewhat surprised to find ourselves waiting for nearly 15 minutes before being seated, despite having a paid and guaranteed reservation. While the restaurant’s popularity, especially over the weekend, is understandable, such a delay does take away slightly from the otherwise premium dining experience one expects with a confirmed booking. In contrast, our weekday visit was handled seamlessly, with immediate seating and a noticeably calmer ambience.

The service on both occasions, however, was exceptional. Every member of the staff was attentive, courteous, and eager to make the experience memorable. A special mention must go to David, who stood out for his warmth and proactive attitude. He went above and beyond to accommodate our preferences, even helping customize certain dishes — a gesture that reflected genuine hospitality and care.

Coming to the food, O Pedro continues to impress with its bold, vibrant flavors. The menu has a unique character — there’s a slight get-used-to element initially, as the dishes often play with contrasting and layered flavor profiles. Overall, the palate leans towards the spicier side, but once accustomed, it becomes quite addictive. Highly recommend trying the Jackfruit Pilaf, the Chorizo Fried Rice (adding an extra egg takes it up a notch), and the Butter Garlic Prawns, all of which stood out for their balance of flavor and quality of preparation.

The ambience, much like the experience, varies by day. On weekends, the place is packed with energy — the crowd is vibrant, the music is loud, and the overall buzz is palpable. While that lends a lively atmosphere, it can get slightly overwhelming when you’re looking for a quieter dining experience.
